decisions_from_product_owner.single_mode: No routine-style concept at all: one mode, the fuller one (2026-10-15).
decisions_from_product_owner.user_trims: The user removes anything extra herself (2026-10-15).
decisions_from_product_owner.removal_in_edit_mode_only: A step is removed only in edit mode so it cannot happen accidentally, in the list and in the calendar (2026-10-15; Q7 yes).
decisions_from_product_owner.regeneration_restores: After the routine is regenerated the removed step is shown again; no persistence of 'user removed this' (no tombstones, no dismissed-steps store) (2026-10-15).
decisions_from_product_owner.gap_card_dismissal_option_b: 'Not for me' on the toner and eye-cream gap cards ONLY, hiding that card until the next save of the routine; cleanser, moisturiser, SPF, pre-cleanse follow-up and mandate cards have no dismissal (Q5, 2026-10-15).
decisions_from_product_owner.left_out_includes_removed: A product removed on purpose still appears in 'Not in your routine' (owned, not hidden on the shelf, no non-hidden saved step in either routine on any weekday). Known trade-off: the list cannot tell removed-on-purpose from never-added (Q6, 2026-10-15).
decisions_from_product_owner.owned_only_engine_input: The engine sees only owned products; wishlist excluded in buildEngineInputFromStores, so live gap cards and the Draft Preview share one input (Q8, 2026-10-15).
decisions_from_product_owner.calendar_discoverability: A caption above the calendar grid and a highlight on the product column make editing from the calendar discoverable (2026-10-15).
decisions_from_product_owner.not_silent: Steps the app calls for (toner, eye cream) are scheduled or raise a visible gap card; an explicit 'Not for me' hides an optional card until the next save and is the user's choice, not an omission; shelf products that miss the routine stay visible with a reason.
decisions_from_product_owner.no_exfoliant_purchase_prompt: No gap card for a missing enzyme exfoliant; an owned enzyme product is still scheduled (Q2, 2026-10-14).
decisions_from_product_owner.clinical_review_deferred: Enzyme values ship as named constants; clinical review after the MVP, before the global release (Q3, 2026-10-14).
decisions_from_product_owner.style_names_moot: Q4a (approved style names) is moot; the retired names must not appear in code, UI copy or tests.

verified_answers.q1_resurrection: Only an explicit Draft Preview save (applyRoutinePlan -> buildStepsFromPlan) or Reset all writes plan-derived steps; validation is a pure read. A removed step is re-created and a hidden step is un-hidden iff the fresh plan schedules the product; otherwise a removed step stays gone and a hidden step stays hidden. Both match her intent: no behaviour change. The code comment claiming hidden steps survive untouched is only true for unplanned products (DOC-2).
verified_answers.q2_gap_cards: The plan, hence the gap cards, is built from shelf + profile only, never from saved steps; an owned toner keeps the slot filled, so removal neither raises nor clears a card. The remaining case (no toner/eye cream owned, deleted, or hidden on the shelf) is now handled by 'Not for me' (Q5 option B).
verified_answers.q3_left_out_membership: Decided YES: listed iff owned, not hidden on the shelf, and no non-hidden saved step in either routine on any weekday; removed and hidden-step products are listed. Supersedes the earlier 'a hidden step counts as saved'.

design_notes.until_next_save: State: AppSettings.dismissedGapCards, at most 4 keys (am|pm x toner|eye_cream), persisted via settingsStore/saveJson (add to pickSettings; hydrate merges the default). 'Next save' = a Draft Preview save clears the keys of the periods it wrote (both, Morning only, Evening only); Reset all clears both; manual add/remove/hide/reorder, shelf edits, period switches and restarts do not. Filter applied after the engine's dedupe (utils gapDismissal: gapDismissKey, visibleGaps, keysAfterSave); only generic toner_recommended / eye_cream_recommended survivors are dismissible. Orchestration in src/domain/routinePlanActions.ts.
design_notes.calendar: RoutineCalendarView stays presentational with optional editMode (default false). Off: neutral caption, no highlight, sheet shows only 'View product details' and 'Edit product'. On: caption 'Tap a product to edit or remove it.', identity column highlighted with statusInfoTint/statusInfoLine (not plum tints, which read pink), sheet shows all four rows. No caption/highlight in the empty state. Row label '<name>, open actions' unchanged (an existing green test needs it) plus a per-mode accessibilityHint.

key_findings: Nothing from the retired style design exists in src/: the deletions are confined to docs and the QA suite.

Wishlist-status products share productsStore.products and the engine has no status check; buildEngineInputFromStores has exactly two callers (generateDraftPlan, validateCurrentRoutines), so one owned-only filter there keeps cards, draft and list in agreement. currentOverrideHash must hash owned ids too.
buildStepsFromPlan writes hidden:false for every planned step, so a hidden step whose product is planned is un-hidden on save; only the unplanned case was tested.
Hiding a product on the shelf drops it silently from the engine, so hiding the only toner raises the toner gap cards and lists nothing (now dismissible with 'Not for me').
routineNoticeDismissedAt cannot give 'until the next save': routineContentHash changes on any add/remove/reschedule and does not change on a no-op save.
Calendar entry limits, unchanged and easier to reach: Remove/Hide act on the product's first visible step (morning before evening) and the 'this weekday only' confirmation names today's weekday.
